transcript.en: It was a terribly persuasive point, and I'd felt disappointed when he said it.
transcript.zh: 这番话极有说服力，而他讲出来的时候，我心里却感到无比失落。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: Also, he denied being a liar. "If I think you're a schmuck," he said, "I'll tell you you're a schmuck." And I believed him. He denied having a parasitic lifestyle. "I'll go get my own meal," he said.
transcript.zh: 此外，他否认自己爱撒谎。“如果我觉得你是个蠢蛋，”他说，“我就会直接骂你是个蠢蛋。”我确实信他这话。他也否认自己过着寄生生活。“我自己去张罗饭吃，”他说。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: And he did have a loyal wife of 41 years.
transcript.zh: 而且，他确实有一位相濡以沫了41年的忠诚妻子。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: There were no rumors of affairs. This would score him a zero on items 17 and 11, many short-term marital relationships and promiscuous sexual behavior.
transcript.zh: 没有任何关于他出轨的流言。这让他在第17项和第11项——“多次短暂的婚姻关系”和“滥交行为”上，都只能得零分。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: We'd had lunch before I left his house. Al had seemed in surprisingly high spirits for a man who'd just been questioned on which psychopathic traits most applied to him.
transcript.zh: 在我离开他家之前，我们一起吃了午饭。对于一个刚被盘问哪条精神变态特征最符合自己的人来说，Al 的兴致出奇地高。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: As we ate, he told me funny stories about firing people. Each was essentially the same: someone was lazy, and he fired them with an amusing quip.
transcript.zh: 吃饭时，他给我讲了些开除员工的趣事。每个故事的情节大同小异：某个人偷懒，然后他用一句妙语把对方炒了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: For instance, one lazy Sunbeam executive mentioned to him that he'd just bought himself a fabulous sports car. "You may have a fancy sports car," Al replied, "but I tell you what you don't have: a job."
transcript.zh: 比如，Sunbeam 有个偷懒的高管跟他说自己刚买了辆超棒的跑车。“你可能买了辆拉风的跑车，”Al 回道，“但我告诉你，你现在没有的是：一份工作。”

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: "You do feel good about yourself?" I asked. "Oh, I do," he replied. "Oh, I do."
transcript.zh: “你自我感觉真的很不错？”我问。“哦，那当然，”他回答，“哦，感觉棒极了。”

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: "Looking back at my life is like going to a movie about a person who did all this stuff. My gosh, I did that. And through it all, I did it my way."
transcript.zh: “回看我的一生，就像在电影院看一个干了这么多大事的人的电影。天哪，那是我干的。而且这一路走来，我都按我自己的方式做到了。”

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: Suddenly, I felt a little envious of him. I am the neurological opposite of a psychopath, in that I feel anxious almost all the time.
transcript.zh: 突然间，我对他竟生出了一丝羡慕。在神经层面上，我完全是精神变态的反面，因为我几乎时时刻刻都在焦虑。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: It must be great to not constantly feel like you've got someone living inside of your face, shooting you with a mini Taser.
transcript.zh: 不用整天觉得有人住在你的脑袋里、拿着迷你电击枪不停电你，那种感觉一定棒极了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: Sure, Al confessed to 16 out of the 40 possible points on the checklist, and you could reasonably give him another six points, which would put him in the 20s, which is high, but not the 29 or 30 which is the clinical line in the sand for psychopathy.
transcript.zh: 诚然，量表上的40分满分里，Al 承认了16分；你客观上还可以再给他加6分，这让他能拿到20多分，这确实很高，但还没达到29或30分——那条判定精神变态的临床警戒线。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: And wouldn't it be nice to just be a little more like him? Someone with no regrets about the past, no remorse, just kind of relaxed and happy?
transcript.zh: 而且，稍微像他一点难道不好吗？一个对过去毫无遗憾、毫无悔恨的人，就那么从容、快活地活着。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Jon Ronson, reading an excerpt from his new book, which is one of the inspirations for today's program, called The Psychopath Test.
transcript.zh: 这是 Jon Ronson，朗读了他新书中的节选。这本书也是我们今天这期节目的灵感来源之一，书名叫《精神变态测试》。

transcript.speaker: Archival Recording
transcript.en: If I were king of the forest, not queen, not duke, not prince. My regal robes of the forest would be satin and not cotton and not chintz.
transcript.zh: （电影《绿野仙踪》唱段）假如我是这片森林的国王，不是王后，不是公爵，也不是王子。我威风的森林华袍该是丝缎，而不是棉布，也不是粗布印花。

transcript.speaker: Archival Recording
transcript.en: I'd command each thing, be it fish or fowl, with a "woof" and a "woof" and a royal growl. As I click my heels, all the trees would kneel.
transcript.zh: （电影《绿野仙踪》唱段）我将号令万物，无论游鱼还是飞鸟，吼一声，再吼一声，发出威严的咆哮。只要我后脚一跺，所有的树木都得跪倒。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Act Three: The Results Are In. Who is the psycho? Thank you for that music cue.
transcript.zh: 第三幕：结果揭晓。谁才是那个精神变态？感谢这段配乐铺垫。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: So if you heard at the beginning of today's program, you heard that I and my fellow producers here at This American Life decided to take the psychopath test ourselves for this week's program. And just to quickly repeat our caveats about that, we did this for entertainment and education purposes only, which meant that we took the short version of the test.
transcript.zh: 如果你听了今天节目的开头，就会知道我和《This American Life》的同事们为了本周的节目，决定亲自测一测这个精神变态测试。再快速重申一下我们的免责声明：我们做这个纯粹是为了娱乐和科普，这也意味着我们测的只是简化版。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: The doctor who administered the test didn't do the kinds of painstaking follow-ups that he normally does. For instance, he didn't look into court records to verify our stories. He took our word for all kinds of things, which he normally would not do if he was facing a real potential psychopath.
transcript.zh: 负责测试的医生并没有像平时那样做严苛细致的背景核实。比如，他没有去查法院记录来验证我们的陈述。他在很多事上都直接听信了我们的一面之词，要是面对真正的潜在精神变态，他绝不可能这么做。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: That's because, um, we assume that none of us was even close to scoring at psychopath levels on the test. We figured that, uh, we would each, you know, score a couple points here, a couple points there, and then we wanted to see who would rack up the most points.
transcript.zh: 这是因为我们都认定，组里没人的分数会接近真正的精神变态水平。我们原本以为大家也就是这里得两分、那里扣两分，纯粹是想看看谁攒的分数最高。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Robyn and Jane, if you remember the beginning of our show, were favorites because of, uh, trouble that they got into as teenagers. Uh, teenage life is a lot of questions on the test. And then there was, uh, one more candidate for scoring points.
transcript.zh: 如果你还记得节目的开头，Robyn 和 Jane 是大家押注的热门，因为她们青春期时惹过不少麻烦——而这个测试里有很多关于青少年时期的问题。另外，还有一个热门候选人。

transcript.speaker: Jonathan Menjivar
transcript.en: I just, I thought if you have the ego to say like, "I'm going to start my own radio show," like, that somehow like you, you, there's, like you just are concentrated more on yourself in a way that would mean that, that you would lean that way.
transcript.zh: 我只是觉得，能有那么大自我膨胀到说“我要做属于自己的广播节目”，那多多少少……就说明你在某种程度上极度以自我为中心，意味着你很可能会往那个方向靠。

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: I thought, I was going to say, you just like are more on the like, feelings stuff.
transcript.zh: 我还以为……我想说的是，你明明更看重“情感共鸣”那一套。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Yeah, the feelings stuff. Yeah, the feelings stuff.
transcript.zh: 对，情感共鸣。是啊，情感共鸣那一套。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Okay, this is going to come as news to anybody who only knows me over the radio, but not news to anybody who knows me in real life. As you might suspect about somebody who designed and created an entire radio show built around very personal conversations and moments where people really connect with each other, the only kind of person who would go to the trouble to invent a show like that would be somebody who, in real life, struggles with every one of those things, which I do.
transcript.zh: 好，对于只通过广播认识我的人来说，接下来的话可能会让人吃惊；但凡是在现实中认识我的人，绝对见怪不怪。正如你对某些人的推测那样——一个精心设计并打造了一整档以极具私密性的深度对话、人与人之间真挚连结为核心的广播节目的人，费尽心机做这事儿的唯一原因，就是他在现实生活中完全搞不定这些事情。而我就是这样。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: I can fake my way through social situations, of course. But people who really know me, like my coworkers do, know how, um, detached and anxious and, um, awkward I can be, which is why they said at the top of the program...
transcript.zh: 在社交场合我当然可以逢场作戏。但真正了解我的人，比如我的同事们，都知道我有时是多么疏离、焦虑和局促，所以他们才会在节目开头那么说……

transcript.speaker: Ben Calhoun
transcript.en: Who do you guys think is going to have the highest score?
transcript.zh: 你们觉得谁得分最高？

transcript.speaker: Nancy Updike
transcript.en: You.
transcript.zh: 你。

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: You.
transcript.zh: 你。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Really?
transcript.zh: 真的吗？

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Sarah Koenig
transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: I, it's a toss-up for me.
transcript.zh: 我……我觉得说不准。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: This is Robyn.
transcript.zh: 这是 Robyn。

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: As I was answering the questions, I kept thinking Jane is going to have such better answers than I am.
transcript.zh: 答题的时候我一直在想，Jane 的答案肯定比我精彩得多。

transcript.speaker: Jane Feltes
transcript.en: That's what I thought, too, because Jane had kind of a more rough-and-tumble...
transcript.zh: 我也这么觉得，因为 Jane 当年的经历要野得多……

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: Law, um... Yeah, like attendance in school and...
transcript.zh: 触犯法律之类的，嗯……对啊，比如学校出勤率还有……

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, I think yeah. I think my money's going on to Jane now. Yeah, yeah.
transcript.zh: 噢，我觉得也是。我现在的赌注全压在 Jane 身上了。是的，没错。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: This by the way is our show's senior producer, Julie Snyder.
transcript.zh: 顺便说一句，说话的是我们节目的资深制作人 Julie Snyder。

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: So now I know more about like Jane's run-ins, I don't know so much about Robyn. I don't know, I like Robyn.
transcript.zh: 所以现在我更了解 Jane 的劣迹了，我对 Robyn 知道得不多。我不知道，我挺看好 Robyn 的。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Robyn, Robyn, what do you got?
transcript.zh: Robyn，Robyn，你有什么料？

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Now I guess I got it between the two of you.
transcript.zh: 现在我想我的选择就在你们俩之间了。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Problems with the law? Let's go to Robyn, Robyn.
transcript.zh: 触犯过法律吗？来听听 Robyn 的吧。

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: No, I have no problems with the law. I have none. I had like one cheating story, which who didn't?
transcript.zh: 没有，我可没触犯过法律。一次都没有。我倒是有过一次作弊经历，但谁还没作弊过呢？

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Cheating story?
transcript.zh: 作弊？

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Cheating on-- you mean on a test?
transcript.zh: 作弊——你是说考试作弊？

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: Um, in school, like, stealing a teacher's manual and lying about it. What? You guys didn't do that?
transcript.zh: 嗯，上学的时候，偷过教师用书还撒谎不承认。怎么，你们都没干过这事？

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Okay. So, let's go around and make our votes.
transcript.zh: 好吧。那我们轮流投个票吧。

transcript.speaker: Jane Feltes
transcript.en: Oh, my god, do we have to?
transcript.zh: 天呐，一定要这样吗？

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: That's Jane, who didn't want to be number one.
transcript.zh: 那是 Jane，她一点也不想当第一名。

transcript.speaker: Jonathan Menjivar
transcript.en: Um, I'm going to go Robyn.
transcript.zh: 呃，我投 Robyn。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Julie?
transcript.zh: Julie 呢？

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Jane.
transcript.zh: Jane。

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: I'm going to go with Jane.
transcript.zh: 我投 Jane。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: I think I think I'm going with Jane.
transcript.zh: 我想我想我也投 Jane。

transcript.speaker: Jane Feltes
transcript.en: If I start crying while you guys are doing this, does that mean I'm not a psychopath?
transcript.zh: 要是你们在这儿投票的时候我哭出来了，是不是就证明我不是精神变态了？

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: In the end, the final tally was Robyn with 4 votes, Jane with 3, I had 1, and, Nancy, in a surprise move, I have to say, voted for herself.
transcript.zh: 最终的计票结果是：Robyn 拿了4票，Jane 拿了3票，我拿了1票。不得不说，Nancy 出了个奇招，她投给了自己。

transcript.speaker: Nancy Updike
transcript.en: I'm in this to win it, I just want to tell you all that. I don't know what game we're playing here, but I'm going to win.
transcript.zh: 我参战就是为了赢，我就想告诉大家这一点。我不知道我们到底在玩什么游戏，但我一定要赢。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Then our forensic psychologist, David Bernstein, joined us. He had actually heard us talking about how worried we were about our scores from the other room.
transcript.zh: 随后，司法心理学家 David Bernstein 加入了我们。他其实在隔壁房间就听到了我们在讨论有多担心自己的得分。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Okay. So you have there like a stack of actually very official looking papers and your notes with all of our scores. Before we get to the actual scores, are there any patterns that you feel like you noticed in the group?
transcript.zh: 好的。你看上去拿了一摞非常正式的报告和手记，上面有我们所有人的分数。在我们揭晓具体分数之前，你觉得你在我们这群人身上有发现什么共同模式吗？

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: Yeah. See, you guys are way too neurotic to really be psychopaths. Interestingly, half of you almost cried as I was asking some of the questions, by the way.
transcript.zh: 是的。看吧，你们都太神经过敏、太焦虑了，根本不可能真是什么变态狂。顺便说一句，有意思的是，在我问某些问题的时候，你们有一半人差点哭出来。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: What?
transcript.zh: 什么？

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: That probably disqualified you from being a psychopath right there.
transcript.zh: 光凭这一点，大概就能直接取消你们当精神变态的资格了。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: David Bernstein explained to us that the way the test is scored, for each of the possible psychopathic traits that you could have, you could get a 0, a 1, or a 2.
transcript.zh: David Bernstein 向我们解释了这个测试的计分机制：针对每一项可能存在的精神变态特质，受试者都会被评为0分、1分或2分。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: 2 means you really have it. 1 means you have it, it's there, but maybe not to the same magnitude. And 0 means it might have been something that occurred, but it's not nearly enough to reach the level of being scored. It's just it doesn't reach that level.
transcript.zh: 2分代表你确实严重具备这项特质；1分代表你有，它确实存在，但可能没那么强烈；0分则意味着即使偶有发生，也远远够不上计分标准。也就是说根本达不到那个严重程度。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: And do you guys want to know what your scores were?
transcript.zh: 那么，你们想知道自己的得分了吗？

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Yeah. Maybe we should start with the lowest scores first and then go to the highest.
transcript.zh: 想。也许我们应该从最低分开始，然后再报最高分。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: Well, this will be very easy, because you all scored a 0. Every one of you.
transcript.zh: 哎呀，那这事可太简单了，因为你们所有人都得了0分。每个人都是。

transcript.speaker: Julie Snyder
transcript.en: Wow. Even Robyn?
transcript.zh: 哇，连 Robyn 也是？

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: Even Robyn.
transcript.zh: 连 Robyn 也是。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: You know, and this is because none of you really did anything maliciously. You never set out to predate, to hurt anyone. And even those of you who've done things, when I asked, how do you feel about it, most of you thought back on it with regret and remorse.
transcript.zh: 你看，这是因为你们谁也没有真正恶意地做过什么。你们从未主动想要去掠夺、去伤害任何人。甚至那些确实做过错事的人，当我问及感受时，大多数人回想起来也充满了后悔与愧疚。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: You're empathic is what you all are, which is the opposite of psychopathy.
transcript.zh: 你们其实都很有同理心，而这恰恰与变态心理背道而驰。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: This is the thing I think we wouldn't have understood as well if we hadn't actually gone through the trouble of taking the test ourselves, is just how categorically different psychopaths are from the rest of us. Dr. Bernstein joked that it's a lifelong commitment.
transcript.zh: 我觉得要不是我们自己费劲亲自做了这套测试，恐怕很难真正理解这一点：那就是变态人格与我们普通人之间，究竟存在着怎样不可逾越的鸿沟。Bernstein 医生还打趣说，那可是一辈子的“执念”。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Even the person who we thought would be the most likely to score a few points on the psychopath test, Robyn, at her most antisocial moment, stealing the teachers manual in junior high school, apparently failed to do what any self-respecting, lacking-in-empathy psychopath would do. This next recording is from when Robyn took the test.
transcript.zh: 就连我们觉得最有可能在测试中拿几分的 Robyn，在她最“反社会”的初中时期偷拿教师用书那次，也完全没做到任何一个有骨气、缺乏同理心的心理变态该做的事。接下来这段录音就是 Robyn 测验时的实况。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: So here's a question. Now, you said you stole you guys stole the manual, and you gave out the answers.
transcript.zh: 那我问你一个问题。你刚才说你们偷了教师用书，然后把答案分发了出去。

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: Yeah. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 对。是的。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: Did you sell the answers?
transcript.zh: 那你卖答案收钱了吗？

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 没有。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: Why'd you give them away?
transcript.zh: 那你干嘛白送人？

transcript.speaker: Robyn Semien
transcript.en: Just because we wanted everyone to do well.
transcript.zh: 纯粹就是希望大家都能考出好成绩嘛。

transcript.speaker: David Bernstein
transcript.en: Mhm.
transcript.zh: 嗯哼。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: That is the "mhm" of "I am bored." That's the "mhm" that you say when you're thinking, "You people are not psychopaths."
transcript.zh: 这一声“嗯哼”，分明写着“真无聊”。那是当你心里嘀咕“你们这帮人根本不配叫变态”时，才会发出的鼻音。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Well, our program was produced today by Jane Feltes with the zero-scoring staff of Alex Blumberg, Ben Calhoun, Sarah Koenig, Jonathan Menjivar, Lisa Pollak, Robyn Semien, Alissa Shipp, and Nancy Updike. Our senior producer is Julie Snyder.
transcript.zh: 今天的节目由 Jane Feltes 制作，全员得零分的幕后团队包括 Alex Blumberg、Ben Calhoun、Sarah Koenig、Jonathan Menjivar、Lisa Pollak、Robyn Semien、Alissa Shipp 和 Nancy Updike。我们的资深制作人是 Julie Snyder。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Production help from Eric Mennel. Seth Lind is our production manager. Emily Condon's our office manager. Jen Berman's filling in as our West Coast producer. Thanks today to Dr. David Bernstein of Forensic Consultants, to Anne Gudencauf and Sean Edens, and to NPR News.
transcript.zh: 制作协助来自 Eric Mennel。Seth Lind 担任制作经理。Emily Condon 是办公室主管。Jen Berman 暂代西海岸制作人。特别鸣谢 Forensic Consultants 的 David Bernstein 医生、Anne Gudencauf、Sean Edens 以及 NPR News。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: Our website, which has all kinds of new features right now, thisamericanlife.org. This American Life is distributed by Public Radio International. WBEZ management oversight for our program by our boss, Mr. Torey Malatia, who wants to move the show, can you believe it, to Louisiana for just one reason.
transcript.zh: 我们的官方网站最近上线了各种新功能，欢迎访问 thisamericanlife.org。《This American Life》由 Public Radio International 发行。来自 WBEZ 的管理监督由我们的大老板 Torey Malatia 负责——你能相信吗？他居然想把节目搬到路易斯安那州去，原因只有一个：

transcript.speaker: Jon Ronson
transcript.en: Alligators. Alligators. More alligators.
transcript.zh: 鳄鱼。全是短吻鳄。成群结队的短吻鳄。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: I'm Ira Glass. Back next week with more stories of This American Life.
transcript.zh: 我是 Ira Glass。下周同一时间，带给你更多《This American Life》的故事。
